lines.japanese: 「お世話さまです！　千歳鷲介、原稿お届けに参りました」
lines.english: “Evening! Shusuke Chitose, here to deliver copy.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぁひっ……？」
lines.english: “Fwah...?”

lines.japanese: 口から春雨ヌードルを垂らしたまま、米田さんが顔をあげました。どうやら軽めの夕食もしくは夜食中だった御様子。
lines.english: Yoneda looked up with glass noodles dangling from her mouth. Apparently I'd caught her in the middle of a light dinner, or perhaps a late-night snack.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ？　今日だっけ？　ちゃー、しまったァ……」
lines.english: “Huh? Was that today? Oh, hell—I really put my foot in it...”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、本人目の前にして、しまったとか言わないでくださいよ」
lines.english: “Come on, don't say ‘damn’ right in front of the person whose appointment you forgot.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あの書類どこにしまったかなあ。そういえば封筒がどこにあるのかも忘れてしまった。まあいいや、しまっていこう！」
lines.english: “Now, where did I put those papers? Come to think of it, I've forgotten where I put the envelopes too. Oh well. Let's put our backs into it!”

lines.japanese: 「や、しまった連呼してもごまかされませんよ」
lines.english: “No. Repeating ‘put’ isn't going to put one over on me.”

lines.japanese: 「それもそうだね、うん。よく考えたら、べつに千歳君なら畏まる必要もないし、このままで問題ないや」
lines.english: “Fair point. Actually, it's only you, Chitose. No need to stand on ceremony. This is fine.”

lines.japanese: あははと笑いながらずるずる春雨をすする米田さん。割り箸を持ってない方の手を伸ばして一言。
lines.english: Yoneda laughed and slurped up her glass noodles. Then she extended the hand not holding her disposable chopsticks and issued a one-word command.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ原稿」
lines.english: “Manuscript.”

lines.japanese: 「くっ、くぬぬ、俺が編集長に密告できるくらいの売れっ子作家なら出し渋ってやるのに」
lines.english: “Ghh... If I were a big enough name to complain to your editor in chief, I'd make you beg for it.”

lines.japanese: しかし今回は、こちらから無理を言って枠をいただいた立場。おとなしく封筒ごと原稿用紙を差しだしました。
lines.english: But I was the one who had begged for this space in the magazine. Meekly, I surrendered the manuscript, envelope and all.

lines.japanese: 「はーい、玉稿いただきましたー」
lines.english: “Very good. Your illustrious manuscript is received.”

lines.japanese: 「一目も通さずに！？」
lines.english: “Without even glancing at it!?”

lines.japanese: 俺の原稿は担当編集の箸を止めることさえなく、春雨ヌードル上空を右から左へと流れていきました。
lines.english: My manuscript sailed from right to left through the airspace above her noodles without once inducing my editor to lower her chopsticks.

lines.japanese: 「え？　ああ、そっか、封筒から出して適当に読むふりぐらいはするべきだったね」
lines.english: “What? Oh, right. I should've taken it out of the envelope and at least pretended to read it.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんごめん、最近アナログ入稿ってホント少ないから、そんな社交辞令すっかり忘れちゃってたよ。やり直そっか？」
lines.english: “Sorry, sorry. Hardly anyone brings in paper copy anymore, so I'd forgotten that little courtesy. Want to try it again?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、いいです……社交辞令とか口にしちゃった時点でぜんぶ台無しなんで……」
lines.english: “No, thanks... The moment you called it a courtesy, the whole performance was ruined...”

lines.japanese: ていうかあの、封筒に汁が飛んでます……。
lines.english: Also, um, there was broth on the envelope...

lines.japanese: 「だってコレ、君の彼女のレビューでしょ？　読まなくたって気合いと情熱のほどは窺いしれるよ」
lines.english: “I mean, this is a review of your girlfriend's book, right? I don't have to read it to know how much fire and passion you poured into it.”

lines.japanese: 「や、仕事っすから、彼女とかそういうのは関係ないすけど。ていうか、そもそも彼女じゃないんで」
lines.english: “No, this is work. Whether she's my girlfriend has nothing to do with it. Also, she isn't my girlfriend to begin with.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　あのとき駅で一緒にいた子が細川玉木ちゃんじゃないの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Wasn't the girl with you at the station Tamaki Hosokawa?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、確かにあのとき一緒だったのは細川玉木ちゃんですが、そもそも彼女じゃないんで」
lines.english: “Yes, the girl with me was Tamaki Hosokawa. She still isn't my girlfriend.”

lines.japanese: 「おっ？　片想いかぁ？」
lines.english: “Oh? Unrequited love?”

lines.japanese: 「ええまあ……相手にもされてないすけど……」
lines.english: “Well, yes... Though she won't even give me the time of day...”

lines.japanese: 「いいねー青少年、悩んどけ悩んどけ。私なんかもう悩むことすら出来ないんだよ。はあ、社会人になったら恋愛なんかしてる暇ないんだもん」
lines.english: “That's youth for you. Agonize, young man, agonize. I can't even agonize over love anymore. Sigh. Once you enter the workforce, there's no time for romance.”

lines.japanese: 「おかしいっすね。世の中には恋愛してる社会人が大勢いるはずですけど。それ単に米田さんの個人的な問題じゃ──」
lines.english: “That's odd. Plenty of working adults seem to find the time for romance. Isn't that simply a personal problem of yours—”

lines.japanese: 「そういえば千歳君、今回は原稿料なくてもいいとか言ってたよね。じゃあ経理にそう言っとくから」
lines.english: “Speaking of which, you said you didn't need a fee this time, right? I'll tell accounting.”

lines.japanese: 「──分かった！　米田さん、仕事できるからすよ！　ほら、男って負けず嫌いだから、デキる女にはつい敵対心持っちゃうんすよ！」
lines.english: “—I get it! It's because you're so good at your job! Men hate losing, so a capable woman naturally inspires hostility!”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、それはあるかもね」
lines.english: “Yes, that may be it.”

lines.japanese: ねえよ、とツッコミを入れるべきか一瞬悩んだものの、原稿料と秤にかけるほどの面白さはないので呑みこんでおきました。
lines.english: For a moment I considered retorting, *No, it isn't*, but the joke wasn't funny enough to risk my fee over, so I swallowed it.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあなに、千歳君もタマキちゃんに惚れる一方、仕事面で嫉妬しちゃってたりするわけ？」
lines.english: “So you're falling for Tamaki and feeling jealous of her professionally at the same time?”

lines.japanese: 「それはないすけど、まあ、釣りあわないなあって弱気になったりはしますよね」
lines.english: “No, not that. But I do get discouraged sometimes, thinking I'm nowhere near her level.”

lines.japanese: 「情けない。だったら彼女に見合う男になればいいじゃない」
lines.english: “Pathetic. Then become a man worthy of her.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすね。精進します」
lines.english: “Right. I'll better myself.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふーん？　言うじゃない。じゃあ期待して待ってるから頑張ってね」
lines.english: “Oh-ho? Listen to you. Then I'll expect great things. Do your best.”

lines.japanese: 「は？　なんで米田さんが期待するんですか？」
lines.english: “What? Why are *you* expecting great things?”

lines.japanese: 「どこからヒットメーカーが生まれるか分からないでしょ。千歳先生もおだてれば木に上るかもよ」
lines.english: “You never know where the next hitmaker will come from. Flatter even a pig and it'll climb a tree—perhaps our budding author will too.”

lines.japanese: 「いま失礼なものに例えましたよね。飛べない俺はただのそれですよね」
lines.english: “You just compared me to something insulting. A pig who can't fly is just a pig, isn't he?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだ、万一大成したら私を娶ってよ。ああ高級住宅街の豪邸で外車乗りまわすなんて最高じゃない？　千歳君にも真珠？」
lines.english: “I know. If by some miracle you make it big, marry me. Imagine it—a mansion in an exclusive neighborhood, foreign cars to drive around. Pearls before Chitose, no?”

lines.japanese: 「また同じものに例えましたよね。そろそろアナタ丸焼きかミンチにしますよ」
lines.english: “You compared me to the same animal again. Keep this up and I'll have you spit-roasted or ground into mince.”

lines.japanese: 「まあまあ、君は楽しくて仕方ない時期なんだから、このくらいの嫌味は許してよ」
lines.english: “Come now. You're in the happiest time of your life. Allow me this much bitterness.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんはちょっと拗ねるみたいに唇を突きだしました。
lines.english: Yoneda gave a small pout.

lines.japanese: 「青春時代の恋愛は、結果いかんに関わらず人生の勉強になるから。気の済むまでタマキちゃんとちゅっちゅしたり喧嘩したり、色々やっときなさい」
lines.english: “Romance in your youth teaches you about life, however it turns out. Make out with Tamaki, fight with her—do whatever you please until you've had your fill.”

lines.japanese: またそうやって大人ぶる……ええ、いいですよ、それではその助言どおり俺は、好きなひとの不安を払うべくお節介を始めさせていただきますとも。
lines.english: There she went, playing the worldly adult again... Very well. Following her advice, I would now commence some meddling to dispel the anxieties of the woman I loved.

lines.japanese: 「てことでお尋ねしますが、その後どーなんすかね、細川玉木の件は？」
lines.english: “Which brings me to a question: what's happened since then with Tamaki Hosokawa?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　どの件？」
lines.english: “What? What do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「彼女の持ち込んだ、最新作『いつだってプリズム』」
lines.english: “Her latest submission, *Always a Prism*.”

lines.japanese: さんざん茶化してたくせに、自社出版物のこととなると途端に渋い顔です米田さん。ビジネスに関わることだから当然っちゃ当然なんだけど、シビアっすねえ。
lines.english: After all that merciless teasing, Yoneda's face turned grim the instant one of her company's books came up. Naturally enough—this was business—but damn, she was hard-nosed.

lines.japanese: 「実はさあ、例のタマキちゃんの担当者──沢井冴子っていうんだけど、そのひと忙しくてそれどこじゃないみたい。書籍の方の同期に聞いた話だと、やっぱり相変わらずだって」
lines.english: “The truth is, Tamaki's editor—Saeko Sawai—is apparently too busy to deal with it. One of my contemporaries in the book division says she's the same as ever.”

lines.japanese: 「目を通してすらいない、って感じすか……」
lines.english: “As in, she hasn't even looked at it...”

lines.japanese: 「いや私もね。沢井さんとは、前に特集組んだときの絡みで何度か話したことあるんだけど、どーもノリが違うというかソリが合わないっていうか」
lines.english: “I've spoken to Sawai a few times myself, back when we ran that feature. But our styles just don't mesh. We rub each other the wrong way.”

lines.japanese: 「前にも言いましたけど……あの、米田さんの方から、なんとか読むだけ読んでもらうよう頼んでもらうのは……やっぱ無理っすよね」
lines.english: “I asked before, but... could you perhaps ask her to at least read it...? No. I suppose that's still impossible.”

lines.japanese: 「前にも言ったけど、ごめんね。さほど親しくもない先輩の方針に、ひよっ子の私が口を出すのもさ」
lines.english: “Like I said, I'm sorry. I'm still just a rookie here. I can't start questioning the policies of a senior I barely know.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは食べおわった容器を捨てると、机に青焼き（平たく言えば誌面の試し刷りです）を広げ、さあ仕事に戻るぞオーラをぶんぶん匂わせ始めました。
lines.english: Yoneda threw away her empty container, spread a blueline across her desk—in plain English, a proof of the magazine page—and began radiating an unmistakable back-to-work aura.

lines.japanese: うーん、米田さんに迷惑はかけたくないけど、俺のツテはこのひとしかいないしなあ。
lines.english: Hmm. I didn't want to make trouble for Yoneda, but she was my only connection here.

lines.japanese: 「え、ええーと、じゃあ読んでくれと直接お願いするわけではなくてですね、その沢井さんってひとが自発的に読みたくなるよう仕向けるってのはどうですかね」
lines.english: “W-well, then. Instead of directly asking her to read it, what if we maneuvered her into wanting to read it herself?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　どうやって？」
lines.english: “What? How?”

lines.japanese: 「や、具体的なプランはまだ考えてないんすけど……」
lines.english: “I haven't thought of a concrete plan yet...”

lines.japanese: 「考えたとしても無理じゃないかなぁ。沢井さんはそういうタイプじゃないんだよ。融通利かないっていうか、仕事に情熱がないっていうか」
lines.english: “Even if you did, I doubt it would work. Sawai isn't that kind of person. She's inflexible—or maybe she just has no passion for the job.”

lines.japanese: 「え、米田さんがそんな風に言うって、どんなひとなんすかその沢井氏」
lines.english: “Coming from you, that's saying something. What kind of person is this Sawai?”

lines.japanese: 「見に行く？」
lines.english: “Want to see?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 米田さんは腰を浮かせると、床の下に指を向けました。
lines.english: Yoneda half rose from her chair and pointed at the floor.

lines.japanese: 「あちらさんもいま忙しいみたいでね。こんな時間だけどまだ残ってたみたいだよ」
lines.english: “Their department is busy too. It's late, but apparently she's still here.”

lines.japanese: この柳木原リベラルビルには六階から十階に祥玄社さんが入っていて、米田さんのいる男性誌編集部は八階にあります。
lines.english: Shogensha occupied floors six through ten of the Yanagihara Liberal Building. Yoneda's *Men's Freeze* department was on the eighth.

lines.japanese: 沢井さんのフロアはその下、七階でした。
lines.english: Sawai worked one floor below, on the seventh.

lines.japanese: 他の階へ足を運ぶのは初めてでしたが、作りやレイアウトはほぼ同じみたいです。
lines.english: It was my first time visiting another floor, but the design and layout looked almost identical.

lines.japanese: スタッフの年齢層は若干上がったかな。みんな忙しそうなのは共通してるけど、パワー溢れるメンフリの編集さんたちより断然静かだ。黙々と働いてて、逆に鬼気迫る感じ。
lines.english: The staff seemed a little older. Everyone looked just as busy, but the floor was far quieter than the high-energy *Men's Freeze* office. They worked in grim silence, which somehow made the intensity worse.

lines.japanese: 「ちっす」
lines.english: “'Sup.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんが遠慮がちなので、なんとなく俺も声を絞ってしまいます。
lines.english: Yoneda sounded unusually diffident, and somehow I found myself lowering my voice too.

lines.japanese: 「うわ、なんかピリピリしてますね。入稿前とかそんなのですか？」
lines.english: “Whoa, the air's tense in here. Are you up against a deadline?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだけど、そうでなくてもここは常にこんな感じ。さ、て、沢井さんは──」
lines.english: “Yes, but this floor's always like this anyway. Now then, Sawai is—”

lines.japanese: フロア内をざっと見渡して眉をひそめる米田さん。
lines.english: Yoneda surveyed the room and frowned.

lines.japanese: 「──あ、あれ？　え、もう帰ってんのかな」
lines.english: “—wait. Huh? Did she already go home?”

lines.japanese: 「いらっしゃらないすか？」
lines.english: “She isn't here?”

lines.japanese: 「おかしいな、そりゃ滅多に残業するようなひとじゃないけど、これだけ他のひとが残ってる状況だから、沢井さんひとりさっさと帰るなんてことはさすがに……」
lines.english: “That's strange. She's hardly the type to work late, but with this many other people still here, surely even Sawai wouldn't be the only one to run off...”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ヨネちゃん。また来たの？」
lines.english: “Oh, Yone. Back again?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: ピンクの煙草ケースを手にした利発そうな女性が、喫煙所方面からやって来ました。
lines.english: A sharp-looking woman approached from the smoking area with a pink cigarette case in one hand.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、よかった沢井さん、まだいらしたんですね」
lines.english: “Oh, good. Ms. Sawai, you're still here.”

lines.japanese: 「もう帰るところだけどね。まだ週も始まったばかりなのに、いつまでも残業なんかしてられないでしょ」
lines.english: “I was just leaving. The week's barely begun. I can't spend every night working late, can I?”

lines.japanese: 「あーハハ、そうっすよねぇ～」
lines.english: “Ah-ha ha. No, of course not.”

lines.japanese: ざっと周囲を見渡してみると、皆さん必死に働いておられます。勇気あるなあ。俺だったら多少無理をしてでも、みんなと足並み揃えちゃうけどなあ。
lines.english: I glanced around. Everyone else was working desperately. She had guts. Me, I'd have pushed myself a little just to keep in step with the group.

lines.japanese: 「で？　今日もまた、なんとか田マキって作家の原稿を勧めにきたワケ？」
lines.english: “So? Are you here to push that manuscript by Whatsername Tamaki again?”

lines.japanese: え？　原稿を勧める？　今日もまた？
lines.english: What? Push the manuscript? *Again?*

lines.japanese: なんだ、米田さんそんなに頑張ってくれてたんだ……いいひとだなあ。
lines.english: So Yoneda had been trying that hard for us... She really was a good person.

lines.japanese: 「あーいえいえ、今日は違うんです。ちょっと若い子に社会科見学させてただけで」
lines.english: “Oh, no, not today. I was just showing a kid how the real world works.”

lines.japanese: 「ど、どぉ～も～」
lines.english: “H-hi.”

lines.japanese: へらへらと頭を下げてみましたが、他部署の外注ライターなんかには興味がないのでしょう。沢井さんとやらは一瞥向けただけで、すぐに米田さんへ視線を戻しました。
lines.english: I bowed with a vacant grin, but she had no interest in some freelance writer from another department. Sawai gave me one glance and turned straight back to Yoneda.

lines.japanese: 「ヨネちゃんもここんとこ、ほとんど泊まりだって？　そんな飛ばしてたら、この先何年もあるんだからもたないよ。自分の時間も作らなきゃ」
lines.english: “I hear you've practically been sleeping here lately, Yone. If you sprint like that, you'll never last through all the years ahead. You need to make time for yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「あ～、しょっちゅう仮眠室は使いますけど、毎日いちおー家には帰ってるっす」
lines.english: “Well, I use the nap room pretty often, but technically I go home every day.”

lines.japanese: 「ヨネちゃん若いねえ。いいけど、どうせあと一年もすれば、がむしゃらにやるよりペースを守ることの方が大事だって気づくと思うよ」
lines.english: “You're young, Yone. That's fine, but give it another year and you'll realize that pacing yourself matters more than charging blindly ahead.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、ご金言ありがたく……」
lines.english: “Ha ha. Words to live by...”

lines.japanese: どうもさっきの口ぶりからすると、米田さん、このひととはそんなに親しい間柄じゃなさそうだったんだけどなあ。少なくとも、説教口調で仕事観を語られるほどには。
lines.english: From the way Yoneda had talked earlier, I hadn't thought she was particularly close to this woman. Certainly not close enough for Sawai to lecture her about work in that tone.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そっか。ヨネちゃんはこの仕事、やっぱりただの腰掛けなのかな」
lines.english: “Oh, I see. Maybe this job really is just something to do until you get married.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、いいんじゃない？　見た目は可愛いんだし、こんな男畑の中で埋もれる前に、早く縁作って結婚しちゃいなよ。この仕事、婚期逃すときついみたいよ」
lines.english: “Why not? You're pretty. Find somebody and marry him before you get buried in this male-dominated field. I hear this job gets brutal once you miss your window.”

lines.japanese: 「いやー、いちおー骨を埋めるつもりではいるんすけどねー」
lines.english: “Well, I do intend to make a career of it.”

lines.japanese: ふうむ。ここまで言うからには、沢井さんはよほど素敵な旦那様をお持ちなのでしょう。だって、見るからに婚期過ぎてるでしょう、他人に結婚観を語るには。
lines.english: Hmm. For Sawai to speak with such confidence, she must have had a truly wonderful husband. After all, she clearly looked past marrying age herself. What standing did she have to lecture anyone else about marriage?

lines.japanese: 「ヨネちゃん、いまオトコいるんだっけ？　あ、もしかしてその若い子──」
lines.english: “Do you have a man right now, Yone? Oh, don't tell me this kid is—”

lines.japanese: そのときひとりの編集さんが立ちあがって、泣きそうな声をおあげになりました。
lines.english: At that moment, one of the editors shot to his feet and cried out in a voice on the verge of tears.

lines.japanese: 「すいませぇーん！　印刷所から問い合わせなんですけど、誰かちょっと手ぇ空いてるひといませんかあ！」
lines.english: “Excuse me! The printing plant has a question! Does anybody have a minute free!?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、まずい、こんなとこいたら帰るタイミング逃しちゃう。じゃあヨネちゃん、何を見学するのか知らないけどごゆっくり。お先失礼」
lines.english: “Oh, damn. If I stay here, I'll miss my chance to escape. Well, Yone, I don't know what you're here to observe, but take your time. See you.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、お疲れさまでーす」
lines.english: “Night.”

lines.japanese: 米田さんと俺を残して、沢井さんは素早くエレベーターに乗りこんでいきました。
lines.english: Leaving Yoneda and me behind, Sawai slipped swiftly into the elevator.

lines.japanese: 「……ん？　あれ？　ひょっとして私の彼氏、コレだと思われた？」
lines.english: “...Hm? Wait. Did she think *this* was my boyfriend?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、ひとに指を向けない」
lines.english: “First, don't point at people.”

lines.japanese: 「そして微妙に顔をしかめない」
lines.english: “Second, don't make that faintly pained face.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、若干羨ましがらせるぐらいの効果はある……かなあ？」
lines.english: “Well, I suppose you'd be enough to make her a little jealous... maybe?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっ、なに言ってんすか！　めちゃめちゃ羨ましがられてますよアナタ！　いまごろ白馬の王子様を射止めた祥玄社のシンデレラと呼ばれてますよ！」
lines.english: “What are you talking about!? She was beside herself with envy! By now she's calling you the Cinderella of Shogensha who landed Prince Charming!”

lines.japanese: へいへい、と歩きはじめた米田さんのあとを追って、メンフリ編集部へ戻りました。
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah,” Yoneda muttered as she started walking. I followed her back to the *Men's Freeze* office.

lines.japanese: 「と、まあ、ああいうひとなワケ」
lines.english: “So. That's the kind of person she is.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、あえて誉めるなら、何者にも臆せず御自分の権利を主張できる、とても強固な意志をお持ちのおねーさんですねえ、と」
lines.english: “Hmm. If forced to praise her, I'd call her a woman of exceptionally firm will who can assert her rights without fear of any person or power.”

lines.japanese: 「合わないでしょ？」
lines.english: “See why we don't get along?”

lines.japanese: 「かもしんないすねえ。自分、対人折衝に関してはわりと気の長い方なんですが」
lines.english: “Maybe. And I consider myself fairly patient when it comes to dealing with people.”

lines.japanese: 「あのひとが今日この時間まで残ってたのも偶然だから。普段は五時きっかりに会社飛びだすタイプ。まあ定時までに自分の仕事をきっかり終わらせてるわけだから、何も間違ってないんだけどね」
lines.english: “Her staying this late today was a fluke. Usually she flies out the door at five on the dot. She gets her own work done precisely by quitting time, so technically she isn't doing anything wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「ですな。しかし、くそう！　せめて自分の担当作家のために、ちょっと時間と労を割いてくれれば！　読んでさえもらえれば、唸らせる自信はあるのに！」
lines.english: “Indeed. But damn it! If only she'd spare a little time and effort for one of her own authors! If we could just make her read it, I'm confident it would make her sit up!”

lines.japanese: 「それは、自分の好きなひとが書いたものだから？」
lines.english: “Because the woman you love wrote it?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「それとも、本当に面白い？」
lines.english: “Or is it truly good?”

lines.japanese: 「んな、後者に決まってるじゃないですか。仮にも相手はプロの編集さんすよ、もしつまんないもんだったら、読んでもらったところでバッサリ斬られるに決まってますって」
lines.english: “The latter, obviously. She's a professional editor. If the manuscript were boring, getting her to read it would only invite her to cut it to ribbons.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、純粋にいい作品なんすよ。決して贔屓目じゃなくて、いやそれも少しはあるかもしんないすけど、でもそれを抜きにしてもお勧めっす。よかったら米田さんもぜひ御一読」
lines.english: “No, it's simply a good book. I'm not blinded by favoritism. Well, perhaps there's a little of that, but even without it, I'd recommend the book without reservation. You should read it too, Yoneda.”

lines.japanese: 「千歳君はここにくると、相変わらず私になにか勧めてくね」
lines.english: “Every time you come here, you try to sell me on something.”

lines.japanese: 「あらら、すいません、つい熱が入っちゃいました」
lines.english: “Oh dear, sorry. I got carried away.”

lines.japanese: 「おっ、一生懸命になってる男の子の顔だ。そういうのお姉さん好きだな」
lines.english: “Oh, there's the face of a boy giving it everything he's got. An older woman like me has a weakness for that sort of thing.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、沢井さんならまだしも、米田さんに好かれたって事態は変わらないしなー」
lines.english: “Well, if Sawai liked me, that might help. You liking me doesn't change our situation, Yoneda.”

lines.japanese: 「言ったな？　よし、米田さんがどれだけ力になれるか見せてやろうじゃん」
lines.english: “You said it. Fine. I'll show you just how useful Yoneda can be.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、どれだけなれるんですか」
lines.english: “What? How useful can you be?”

lines.japanese: 「分かんないけど、出来るかぎりの協力はさせてもらうよ。その代わり、上手くいったら一生恩に着せるけどね」
lines.english: “No idea, but I'll help however I can. In return, if this works, I'll hold it over you for the rest of your life.”

lines.japanese: 「まじすか！　そんなんでいんすか！　いやっはー、なんていいひとなんでしょ米田さん」
lines.english: “Seriously!? That's all you want? Yes! Yoneda, what a magnificent human being you are!”

lines.japanese: 「恋愛とその喪失は、人間としての視野を広げるからね。未来ある若者の成長を助けてあげるのも担当編集の仕事ってカンジ？」
lines.english: “Love—and losing it—broaden a person's horizons. Helping a promising young man grow is part of an editor's job too, I suppose.”

lines.japanese: 「アレッ！？　なんで失恋前提！？」
lines.english: “Wait! Why is heartbreak a foregone conclusion!?”

lines.japanese: 「たまには、若さと勢いだけで勝算のない戦に突っ走れるタフさもいいけど──」
lines.english: “There is something to be said for the toughness of youth—the ability to charge into a hopeless battle on youth and momentum alone—”

lines.japanese: 「アレッ！？　いま勢いだけって言った？　勝算のない戦って言った！？」
lines.english: “Wait! Did you say vigor alone? Did you call it a battle I can't win!?”

lines.japanese: 「──大きな悲しみを乗りこえたあとの人間は、物事の本質を見抜ける目が養われるよ。一回り成長して、物書きとしての階段もとんとん上がってねぇん」
lines.english: “—but once people overcome great sorrow, they develop an eye for the heart of things. Grow a little wiser and climb the ladder as a writer while you're at it, hmm?”

lines.japanese: おじぎをして編集部から去ると、ビルの外は驚くほど冷たい空気。思ったより体が温まっていたようです。
lines.english: I bowed and left the editorial office. Outside the building, the air was astonishingly cold. Apparently I'd gotten warmer than I realized.

lines.japanese: 「物書きとしての、か……」
lines.english: “As a writer, huh...”

lines.japanese: いつもは米田さんが軽く口にするだけの「千歳先生」って言葉が、なんだかくすぐったく感じられました。
lines.english: Yoneda was always teasingly casting me as some great author, but tonight the idea left me feeling strangely self-conscious.

lines.japanese: なあんて、ちょっと将来のようなものを考えてしまう夜のこと。
lines.english: It was the kind of night that made me think, just for a little while, about something resembling a future.
